question: Which of the following results in increase in secretion of ADH?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hypovolemia" -> "decreased blood volume" -> "increased plasma osmolarity" -> "stimulation of osmoreceptors" -> "increased secretion of ADH" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hypervolemia" -> "increased blood volume" -> "decreased plasma osmolarity" -> "inhibition of osmoreceptors" -> "decreased secretion of ADH" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Hypertension" -> "increased blood pressure" -> "possible activation of baroreceptors" -> "inhibition of ADH secretion" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Decrease osmolarity" -> "lower concentration of solutes in plasma" -> "inhibition of osmoreceptors" -> "decreased secretion of ADH" -> 90%
analysis: The secretion of ADH (antidiuretic hormone) is primarily influenced by plasma osmolarity and blood volume. In conditions of hypovolemia, there is a decrease in blood volume, which leads to an increase in plasma osmolarity. This triggers osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus to stimulate the release of ADH from the posterior pituitary gland. Conversely, hypervolemia and decreased osmolarity both lead to a decrease in ADH secretion, as they signal sufficient or excess fluid in the body. Hypertension can also inhibit ADH secretion through baroreceptor activation. Therefore, the only condition that results in an increase in ADH secretion is hypovolemia, which aligns with established physiological principles. Thus, the best-supported option is hypovolemia.
